messages:
marta: Heads up — started seeing a surge of SCIM 403s after the RBAC roll yesterday. Affected service accounts only, not full org. Logs show signature verification failed on the SAML/OIDC side. Anyone else seeing this?

devin: Can you paste the assertion header or id_token header you’re seeing? also, did we rotate any signing keys or KMS keys recently?

marta: here’s the id_token header from one failed call: `{"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT","kid":"staging-key-2026"}`

and SCIM response: `403 {"error":"invalid_signature","detail":"signature verification failed"}`

henry-sec: HS256 in the header is a red flag — our SP expects RS256 (jwks-based). That can happen if the IdP fell back to client-secret (symmetric) signing, or if metadata/jwks is absent so the provisioning app used an alternate flow. Check idp metadata + JWKS endpoint first.

linda-ops: we ran a scheduled KMS key rotation ~2h ago (job id: rotate-keys-2026-04-01). Not intentional to touch signing config, but the rotation script touched the idp service env in the same deploy. Investigating.

marta: interesting — RBAC change was also rolled at ~1:30, removed scim:write from a role, but only service accounts tied to the provisioning app are failing. Role change wouldn’t normally flip alg though.

devin: agreed RBAC removal wouldn’t change signing alg. More likely: cert/key missing from SP metadata caused IdP to fallback. Run these checks: 
```
curl -s https://idp.prod.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration
curl -s https://idp.prod.example.com/jwks.json | jq '.keys[].kid'
```

henry-sec: also check KMS audit for encrypt/decrypt/sign calls around the rotation window: `gcloud kms keys versions list --key=redwood-idp-signing --location=global` and `gcloud logging read 'resource.type=cloud_kms' --limit 50`

marta: ran jwks curl — it returned `{"keys":[]}` (empty array). Metadata URL returns correct issuer but jwks is empty.

linda-ops: ack — the rotation job accidentally set IDP_JWKS_HOST to `idp.staging.internal` in the prod env for the provisioning service. That explains empty JWKS. I only noticed after the alerts. I’ll revert the env var and re-run the metadata sync. Sorry. :grimacing: 

deploy-bot: deploy started for service provisioning (job: revert-jwks-host-1782)

devin: immediate mitigation options: 1) revert env var (good), 2) re-set the previous KMS key as active for signing if the rotation changed key alias, or 3) temporarily enable client secret fallback for that app (least preferred). Plan for a quick revert + verify JWKS populated then test provisioning.

henry-sec: once reverted, we should: (a) check KMS audit to confirm no unauthorized sign operations, (b) add an alert if jwks.json returns empty or contains no keys, (c) add a canary test that exercises SCIM provisioning after infra changes. I’ll open a short runbook snippet.

marta: reversion in progress — I’ll validate SCIM after deploy completes and post logs.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded (revert-jwks-host-1782) — 1718923528

marta: quick update — JWKS now returns two keys: `["prod-key-1","prod-key-0"]`. Provisioning retries succeeded for the failing service accounts, SCIM jobs are progressing.

linda-ops: confirmed we’ll pause automated rotations for the idp signing alias until we have a safe migration path. I’ll also add a preflight check to the rotation job to validate metadata endpoints.

henry-sec: marking this as sev3 for now, but we should treat as a near-miss. I’m adding an audit-bot alert rule: `if jwks.keys | length == 0 then pager` and a follow-up postmortem action item list.

audit-bot: alert-rule created: jwks-empty -> pager (threshold=1, owner=eng-security)

marta: thanks all — provisioning fixed, will create a short postmortem (root cause: rotation job mis-set env var pointing prod to staging JWKS), action items: preflight, pause automated rotations, add canary.

henry-sec: please include timeline and bullets for remediation; I’ll add recommended RBAC checks in the PM.

marta: will do — closing thread once postmortem published.
